recognize_zh: 周邊血抹片紅血球之間可見一條細長、呈規則波浪狀捲曲的螺旋菌（spirochete），位於細胞外、長度約 1–2 個紅血球直徑，配合高燒與低血壓，即為回歸熱螺旋體（Borrelia）菌血症。
features: Single thin, extracellular, loosely coiled spiral organism between red cells
Organism length roughly 1-2 red cell diameters with regular undulations, staining lightly purple
Red cells show mild anisocytosis without significant fragmentation
A band/segmented neutrophil without intracellular organisms
Platelets not prominent in this field
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows red cells with mild anisocytosis and an occasional neutrophil. A thin, extracellular spirochete with regular, loose coils is present in the plasma between red cells. No intraerythrocytic parasites or intracellular inclusions are identified in this field. In a febrile, hypotensive patient, findings are consistent with spirochetemia due to relapsing fever Borrelia (e.g. Borrelia hermsii).

ddx.dx: Fibrin strand or stain precipitate artifact
ddx.vs: Artifacts are irregular, variably thick and lack the uniform regular coils of a spirochete.
Trypanosomes are larger with a visible nucleus, kinetoplast and undulating membrane, unlike this slender coiled organism without internal structure.
Leptospires are finer with tightly wound coils and hooked ends and are rarely seen on Wright-stained smears.
Microfilariae are much larger (many red cells long) with a column of nuclei.
